clauses.reason: The command is: "I hereby amend Executive Order No. 10349 of April 26, 1952 ... by striking out 'June 1, 1952' appearing in the introductory paragraph of the order and inserting in lieu thereof 'June 15, 1952'." Text before: "June 1, 1952". Text after: "June 15, 1952". Executive Order 10362 then struck "June 15, 1952" and inserted "June 30, 1952", and Executive Order 10367 struck "June 30, 1952" and inserted "July 3,1952". These are amendments, which are later events and not ends; the clause continued, amended. The period ended with its last stated day, July 3, 1952, recorded inclusive (the exclusive reading would be July 2, 1952). No later held order changes it. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory records the order as one whole clause without isolating the operative words. The operative command is the single sentence from 'By virtue of the authority' to 'June 15, 1952.': the President amends Executive Order No. 10349 of April 26, 1952 by striking out 'June 1, 1952' in its introductory paragraph and inserting 'June 15, 1952'.

research_rationale:
EO 10356 (17 FR 4967; signed May 29, 1952; F.R. Doc. 52-6133) amends Executive Order No. 10349 of April 26, 1952, which declared the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service a military service for a stated period, by striking out "June 1, 1952" and inserting "June 15, 1952". The amended date was changed twice. Executive Order 10362 (signed June 14, 1952) struck "June 15, 1952" and inserted "June 30, 1952", and Executive Order 10367 (signed June 30, 1952) struck "June 30, 1952" and inserted "July 3,1952". Under the 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling these amendments are later events that record the before and after text, and the clause continues, amended, until the amended period ends. The last held date in the introductory paragraph is July 3, 1952. The introductory paragraph of Executive Order No. 10349 (held in the corpus but not registered as evidence in this packet) states the period as running to and including its end date, so July 3, 1952 is recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading would end the period on July 2, 1952. No held order after EO 10367 changes the date. The two amending orders are government printed Federal Register copies registered in the packet.
